Hi all - quick technical clarification and an adjusted unit economics example.

1) Tokens vs characters vs requests
- Token unit: tokens are subword pieces used by the model. A practical conversion is ~4 characters per token for typical English text, but it can vary (short words and punctuation increase token count). Use 4 chars/token as a conservative estimate for planning.
- Requests = API calls. Each request's billed tokens = input_tokens + output_tokens (unless a cached prefix entirely prevents sending that text to the model; see below).

2) Prompt / prefix caching and billed tokens (how Redwood handles it)
- Default hosted behavior: we bill for tokens that are sent to the model. If you send the full prompt every time (system + user), we bill for that input plus the generated output.
- Prefix (prompt) caching: Redwood offers an enterprise prefix-caching option. When enabled, we keep a cached representation of the static prefix (system prompt / template) on the serving side. For cache hits where the cached prefix is not re-sent to the model, we do not bill customers for the cached prefix tokens - you are billed only for the dynamic portion (user prompt) and output tokens. There are caveats: cache hit depends on determinism of the prefix and context; very dynamic templating reduces hit rates.
- KV/response caching: for some workflows where we can return cached responses (100% hit), you are billed only for the request handling (negligible) and not for model tokens. These are corner cases.

3) Sanity-check the numbers and corrected calc (using conservative assumptions)
Assumptions: 4 chars/token; per-request chars = system 1,200 (cacheable) + user 250 (dynamic) + output 600 (generated); cache hit rate for system prompt: 95% (enterprise prefix caching).
- Tokens per request (if no caching): 2,050 chars / 4 ~ 513 tokens.
- With prefix caching and 95% hit on the 1,200-char prefix: billed tokens per request ~ ((user + output) chars)/4 + (5% * prefix_chars/4) ~ (850 / 4) + (0.05 * 1,200 / 4) ~ 212.5 + 15 ~ 228 tokens/request.
- Monthly tokens at 150k requests: 150,000 * 228 ~ 34.2M tokens/month.

Pricing example (pick $/1M token to show ranges):
- At $20 / 1M tokens -> 34.2 * $20 ~ $684/month
- At $40 / 1M tokens -> 34.2 * $40 ~ $1,368/month
- At $10 / 1M tokens -> 34.2 * $10 ~ $342/month

Observations:
- The difference between counting characters vs tokens can create big swings; converting chars->tokens with 4 chars/token is a good planning heuristic.
- Prefix caching materially lowers billed tokens if the static portion is large and hit rates are high (see calc above).
- Ask: leadership's $3k-6k/month target is achievable if either the effective $/1M token is in the $20-40 range with these volumes or if volumes are lower. With a 34M token/month run rate, $3k would imply an effective price ~ $87 / 1M (not likely for self-serve list prices), so confirm whether the $3k-6k includes other infra or usage tiers, or whether they expect a large discount as part of a committed Dedicated contract.

Next steps I recommend:
- Marissa / Acme: confirm expected pilot month requests (150k accurate?) and expected cacheability of your system prompt (is it deterministic templates or per-user dynamic substitutions?).
- If prefix is deterministic, we can model a conservative hit rate (e.g., 80-95%) and send a refined estimate.
- If you want, we can provision a short sandbox test where we instrument token counts from a sample of 10k requests to measure real-world chars->tokens and cache hit rates. That gives accurate billing projections.

Marissa - feel free to copy/paste this back to Alex. Alex & Priya - happy to run the sandbox if you can share a representative sample or approve a short test run.
